question: Did fixing the split flatten the exposure gradient?
answer: NO. The gap widened. See interpretation.
interpretation: The exposure gradient measures OVERFITTING, not leakage. Repairing the split does not reduce overfitting; it makes it honestly visible.
The inherited gradient understated the gap because its unseen estimate rested on 5 SC-only subjects with kappa spread 0.435-0.724 - a small, favourable draw.
The retrained gradient rests on 15 held-out subjects including 3 ST, a broader and harder sample.
The retrained model also saw less data (137 vs 157 recordings) and trained to a lower loss (0.05), so it does overfit somewhat harder.

head_to_head_on_test_split.note: The inherited teacher trained on 14 of these 15 subjects, so its aggregate is contaminated.

only_valid_head_to_head.subject: SC474
only_valid_head_to_head.why: the only subject unseen by BOTH models
only_valid_head_to_head.conclusion: Statistically indistinguishable at n=1. The inherited teacher was never better; it was better measured.

entropy.note: Retrained is MORE confident (lower entropy) while being LESS accurate on this split - i.e. worse calibrated. Relevant to Phase 7.

cohort.note: ST is harder for both. This is the first clean ST measurement in the project.
